scope.explanation: Use evidence to choose parameter, causal-feature, permitted device-weight, or composite controls. Labels, sampling, feature_set, schedule and scorer remain fixed.

feature_api.input: One device, chronological numeric rows. No labels, device IDs or future rows. Select literal column names from profile.feature_names.
feature_api.output: pd.DataFrame of declared unique fe_ columns; preserve rows and index. Original columns are retained automatically.

past_helpers.past.gap_seconds(frame): Series: current minus previous observation time in seconds; first value NaN.
past_helpers.past.observation_count(frame): Series: causal count 1,2,...,n; no measured-value missingness dependence.

rules: Only assignments to new local names and a final return. No loops, comprehensions, imports or arbitrary functions.
frame.index is permitted ONLY as index=frame.index in pd.DataFrame. For time gaps use past.gap_seconds(frame).
No frame.columns, to_series, dt, iloc, loc, values, pd.Series, pd.to_numeric or apply. Inputs are already numeric.
Use arithmetic operators / + - * instead of .div/.add/.sub/.mul. Use literal column names; never discover columns dynamically.
Reductions must directly follow rolling/expanding/ewm. Use trailing real-time rolling windows; center=True and negative shifts are forbidden.
Missing measurements stay unknown unless the hypothesis explicitly justifies a constant or forward fill. No infinities.
Zero finite values in a bounded sample is a coverage limitation, not evidence that the entire dataset is empty.

hypotheses.mechanism: Grown surface defects trigger spare-sector reallocation, consuming the spare pool and indicating media degradation.
hypotheses.basis: Backblaze Drive Stats and published SMART studies identify SMART 5 raw reallocated sector count as one of the strongest failure predictors; normalized value declines as spare sectors are consumed.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Pre-failure devices do not show higher raw reallocated counts and lower normalized values than healthy devices at comparable lead times.

hypotheses.mechanism: Unstable sectors await remapping, producing current pending sectors that may later become uncorrectable.
hypotheses.basis: Backblaze data shows SMART 197 raw pending sector count above zero strongly increases failure probability.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Failing devices do not have elevated smart_197_raw counts in the prediction window compared with healthy devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: Uncorrectable read/write errors reflect media, head, or channel failure that cannot be recovered by ECC.
hypotheses.basis: SMART 187 reported uncorrectable errors are widely associated with imminent HDD failure in reliability studies.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Reported uncorrectable error counts are not higher in failing devices than healthy devices before failure.

hypotheses.mechanism: Frequent remapping attempts indicate active defect growth, even if reallocated sector total remains moderate.
hypotheses.basis: SMART 196 reallocated event count captures the number of remap operations and is a known failure precursor.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Reallocated event counts do not differentiate failing from healthy devices within the lead window.

hypotheses.mechanism: Drive unresponsiveness from firmware, head, or media issues manifests as command timeouts.
hypotheses.basis: Operational experience shows accumulating SMART 188 command timeouts often precedes total drive failure.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Failing devices do not show higher command timeout counts than healthy devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: Increased ECC recovery activity indicates marginal read channels and deteriorating media signal quality.
hypotheses.basis: SMART 195 hardware ECC recovered counts rise when drives must correct many errors, a known degradation indicator.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Hardware ECC recovered counts are not elevated in failing devices after controlling for workload.

hypotheses.mechanism: Actuator or servo instability causes seek errors before mechanical failure.
hypotheses.basis: SMART 7 seek error rate is associated with positioning degradation, a common near-failure signature.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Seek error rate does not increase in failing devices relative to healthy devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: Spindle or motor difficulty causes repeated spin-up attempts.
hypotheses.basis: SMART 10 spin retry count captures motor start problems, a mechanical failure precursor.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Failing devices do not have higher spin retry counts than healthy devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: Age-related wear increases failure probability after high power-on hours, though risk is not strictly monotonic.
hypotheses.basis: HDD reliability follows a bathtub curve: infant mortality, then steady wear-out at high power-on hours.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Failure risk is not elevated at extreme high power-on hours after controlling for drive model and cohort.

hypotheses.mechanism: Repeated head load/unload cycles mechanically wear the actuator and ramp, increasing late-life failure risk.
hypotheses.basis: Load/unload cycle count, especially on 2.5-inch drives, is a mechanical wear indicator.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Failing devices do not show accumulated load cycle counts different from healthy devices at similar age.

acceptance_rule.explanation: best changes only when paired CV bootstrap 95% lower bound > lower_bound and net hits are not lost

task_context.instructions: Domain-adapted evidence loop: separate false alarms, missed faults and coverage; allow bounded interaction/recall feature exploration, single-factor device weights and optional independent parallel branch. Reuse the source sampling policy and fixed evaluation. New source/representation requires a new cache/session. TEST stays outside search.
